#### 1. hypertriglyceridemia 2  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8963889)

**Proposed mechanism:** LIPC (HGNC:6597) —DISRUPTS→ Lipid Metabolism (GO:0006629); CREB3L3 (HGNC:26697) —DISRUPTS→ Lipid Metabolism (GO:0006629); Lipid Metabolism (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Hepatomegaly (HP:0002212); Lipid Metabolism (GO:0006629) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertriglyceridemia (HP:0002118). Loss-of-function variants in LIPC (causative for Cholesterol ester storage disease) and CREB3L3 (causative for hypertriglyceridemia 2) both converge on the disruption of the broader lipid metabolism pathway, leading to distinct but related phenotypic consequences.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in LIPC and CREB3L3 affect entirely distinct and non-interacting sub-modules within the broader lipid metabolism pathway, such that perturbations in one do not influence the other's phenotypic outcome. _(variant: Presence of common variants (>1% allele frequency) in gnomAD within the coding regions of LIPC and CREB3L3 that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of lipid metabolism disruption in these diseases could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common metabolic pathways for both conditions, potentially improving treatment efficacy and broadening applicability.

Loss-of-function mutations in APOC2 (Disease B) directly impair the activation of lipoprotein lipase, leading to impaired triglyceride hydrolysis and chylomicronemia.
